text:
mohan: @here customer reporting a surge-related issue — starting ~2026-03-09T09:00Z they saw ~15% 429s and elevated p95 for generation across EU region. Traffic came from both us-west and eu-west. sample request ids: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c3e. Any quick triage ideas? :rotating_light:

hana: can you drop a minimal repro and the model & project id? also share any headers like X-RateLimit-* if available.

mohan: minimal repro below (redacted key). they were using rw-14b in hosted mode. project id: proj-abc123.
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXXXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-14b","input":"summarize: test","max_new_tokens":64}'
```
I also captured response headers from one failed request: `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `Retry-After: 5`, and body: `{ "error": "regional_capacity_exceeded", "region": "eu-west" }`.

maria: saw same from a different customer — they triggered a simultaneous fanout from multiple AZs. docs mention fallback but behavior seemed inconsistent: some requests spilled to us-west and succeeded, some still 429'd. console shows tenant routing: `affinity: eu-prefer` for proj-abc123.

kevin: short summary of how routing works today: per-tenant we maintain region affinity + reserved regional pools. If a tenant allows geo-fallback and model variant is available elsewhere, we route to alternate region. Dedicated customers or tenants with `affinity: region-strict` do NOT fallback. There's also a global overflow pool but the scheduler applies admission control/credit checks. If credits exhausted you get `regional_capacity_exceeded`.

sam: pulling logs from the time window. snippet: 
```
2026-03-09T08:59:59Z scheduler INFO accept req_id=r-0a1b2c3d tenant=proj-abc123 region=eu-west pool=reserved
2026-03-09T09:00:12Z scheduler WARN backpressure start window=120s region=eu-west
2026-03-09T09:00:12Z router ERROR route_fail req_id=r-0a1b2c3d reason=regional_capacity_exceeded dst_region=eu-west
2026-03-09T09:00:12Z router INFO attempt_fallback req_id=r-0a1b2c3d dst_region=us-west outcome=queued
2026-03-09T09:00:14Z router ERROR fallback_fail req_id=r-0a1b2c3d reason=no_available_slots
2026-03-09T09:00:15Z gateway INFO resp req_id=r-0a1b2c3d code=429
```
That sequence shows scheduler/backpressure plus fallback attempts that never found slots.

support-bot: [automated] Alert: region eu-west capacity > 90% at 2026-03-09T09:00:10Z — linked runbook https://console.redwood.ai/ops/runbooks/regional-capacity

hana: thx, that's helpful. two immediate asks for customer: 1) enable geo-fallback for the tenant if they can accept cross-region routing (console link below), 2) add 429 retry with jitter and exponential backoff, honor `Retry-After`. Example client guidance: 
```js
// pseudocode
if (resp.status === 429) {
  wait = parseInt(resp.headers['retry-after'] || 2) * 1000;
  await sleep(wait + jitter());
  retry();
}
```

maria: customer asked about billing/quota implications when fallback occurs — will they be billed differently if a request routes to another region?

kevin: short answer: no surprise double-billing for a single request. Billing is per successful token generated. However, note differences between Hosted vs Dedicated pricing buckets — if a fallback routes into a Dedicated pool for a different tenant type, that could be a different cost profile (rare). Quotas: we enforce some counters per-region and per-account; enabling fallback will cause consumption to touch multiple regional counters, but we count tokens once for billing.

mohan: is there a quick server-side mitigation we can flip while infra digs into scheduler? e.g., bump overflow admission or extend burst credits?

sam: I can temporarily increase the scheduler admission window and surge credits for eu-west for the tenant namespace `proj-abc123` and bump global overflow threshold. Doing now — will post what I changed. pinging @eng-oncall.

kevin: longer-term root cause: correlated fanout + admission window too tight + tenant region affinity. Action items: 1) adjust default admission controller thresholds to reduce false positives on short spikes, 2) add clearer console flag `allow_cross_region_fallback` with defaults and warning text, 3) add alert that surfaces `% of fallback_attempts_failed` for a region.

maria: customer accepted enabling fallback for now and implementing retry logic client-side. they also asked for repro steps so they can test after changes — can we provide a step-by-step?

mohan: yes — repro steps for them: 1) enable geo-fallback: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/proj-abc123/routing, 2) send 100 concurrent POSTs with small payload to /v1/generate from two different regions (I used k8s jobs in us-west and eu-west), 3) observe headers `X-Route-Region` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and confirm fallback responses have `X-Fallback-Used: true` when applicable. Example curl loop we shared earlier.

sam: infra note: I opened PR #842 on scheduler to relax burst admission for 120s windows -> 180s on short spikes, and added an integration test simulating cross-zone fanout. will roll canary tonight.

kevin: I'll add a quick dashboard tile to show `regional_capacity_exceeded` counts by tenant and region + a graph of fallback success ratio.

maria: thanks all, I'll relay to customer and confirm after they run their test. :thumbsup:

mohan: great — I'll follow up with a short summary and close with the customer once they validate. tagging this as follow-up: docs, infra patch, monitoring.
